newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia stocks trend lower, HK takes a breather.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks trend lower, HK takes a breather.

text.p: Asia stocks trended lower on Friday, with a retreat in London and New York market's overnight setting the tone for the region ahead of the release of key U.S. employment data due later on Friday.
The mood was particularly evident in Hong Kong, where the key Hang Seng index slipped after winning a hard fought battle to top the key 12,000 level on Thursday.
"It will probably consolidate its recent gains. There are important U.S. figures coming out...," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Hang Seng Index was off 20.57 points, or 0.17 percent, at 11,993.99.
Despite the drop, dealers were optimistic about further gains in the Index, which advanced for seven straight days and tacked on 225 points this week alone.
"We still see some upside for the index, although the market is likely to take a breather today," said Angus Shillington of institutional sales at Asia Equity.
In London, the FTSE-100 set another record on Thursday but retreated slightly as traders turned cautious until after release of the U.S. employment figures for September.
After touching 4,024.3, the FTSE eased to 4,000 points, to end 15.1 points, or 0.04 percent lower.
Similarly, a mild bout of profit-taking snapped the Dow Jones Industrial Average's four day rally on Thursday, leaving the Dow off 1.12 at 5,932.85 on Thursday.

The Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged for now and other recent economic data have taken some of the usual intense focus off September's figures, although that could change if they fall wide of economists forecasts.

Economists polled by Reuters in New York look for the creation of 166,000 new jobs in September, down from 250,000 in August. How much workers earn on an average hourly basis -- a key barometer of inflation prospects -- are expected to rise 0.2 percent in September after rising 0.5 percent a month earlier.
In Tokyo, shares trended lower as sentiment was sapped by the weak performance of overseas markets and the drop in Tokyo shares on Thursday.
The key Nikkei 225-share average was off 199.64 points, or 0.94 percent, at 21,131.86 at midday there.

Shares in the Philippines made a dramatic recovery before the close after a broker stepped in and bought up shares of blue chip Ayala Land, a victim of a shakeout in the property sector. After being down more than a point, the Manila stock index closed 0.88 points, or 0.03 percent, higher at 3,131.14 points.
In Seoul, shares were lower, pressured by mounting tensions on the Korean peninsula after Pyongyang threatened to retaliate over a submarine incident.
The composite index was off 6.56 points, or 0.83 percent, at 787.85.

In Thailand, traders said heavy selling led by fund managers in Hong Kong brought the market down more than two percent. Stock have been declining steadily due to political unrest that resulted in a call for elections in November.
The Jakarta Composite Index was off 2.667 points, or 0.45 percent, at 587.123 points.

In Singapore, where the focus shifted to Malaysian stocks traded over the counter, the Straits Times Index was off 4.12 points, or 0.19 percent, at 2,146.64. The Kuala Lumpur composite index was up 8.51 points, or 0.74 percent, at 1,156.23.
Taiwan proved the exception to most of Asia, with its key index adding 4.63 points, or 0.07 percent, to reach a new 1996 closing high of 6,616.21.
